text:
alex: Seeing a retry spike for gpu-serving pods in us-west-2 (inference-gpu svc). ~8% 5xx and some client-side retries. Anyone seeing this?

maria: Yep, dashboards show traffic skewed to two endpoints in that svc. ipvs stats look uneven — one endpoint getting most connections.

jordan: Did we change any routing/MTU configs last night for the GPUPool?

alex: We rolled jumbo frames to 9000 on the new gpu nodes overnight, but older gpu nodes stayed at 1500. Could be path MTU mismatch.

vikram: I ran quick tcpdump on gpu-03 and saw lots of fragmentation and retransmits between pods. Also saw RDMA-enabled NICs on that host (mlx5). Sample kernel logs mention ipvs warnings.

alex: infra-bot shows kube-proxy restarted on gpu-03 at ~00:11 UTC, maybe related.

infra-bot: ALERT: kube-proxy crashloop on gpu-03 (restart_count=4) at 1782456800

maria: Can someone paste `ip -d link show` and ipvs stats from gpu-03? I'll check kube-proxy flags too.

jordan: ```
# on gpu-03
ip -d link show dev vxlan0
2: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    vxlan id 1000 remote 0.0.0.0 srcport 0 dstport 4789

# ipvs snapshot
Proto LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  TCP 10.0.5.12:8080 rr persistent 
  -> 10.0.3.45:8080 masq weight 1 activeconn 9876 inactconn 12
  -> 10.0.3.46:8080 masq weight 1 activeconn 123 inactconn 4
```

vikram: That mtu 1450 on vxlan0 is interesting — overlay reduced available payload; if underlying NICs are at 9000 and some at 1500, fragmentation happens at different layers. RDMA offloads (GSO/GRO) can coalesce/skew skb metadata which affects ipvs hash calculation in older kernels (seen on 5.15 series).

alex: Short-term mitigation ideas? change ipvs scheduler, reconciling MTU, or disable GSO/GRO on suspect NICs?

maria: Scheduler tweak is risky. Safer: make MTU consistent and/or disable GSO/GRO on problematic VF to force consistent skb layout. I can try `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off` on one node as test.

jordan: Did that on gpu-03 just now and bumped vxlan0 -> 9000 to match the pool. After toggling off GRO/GSO, I see reconnects drop and ipvs distribution more even in the next minute.

alex: Post-change metrics: retries down from 8% -> 0.7% in 10m window. Good sign.

vikram: Confirmed in kernel logs: after disabling GSO we stopped hitting the ipvs hash collision bug. Short-term fix works. Will draft kernel backport note for 5.15/6.x kernels in case of upgrades.

maria: Runbook draft (short):
1) Validate MTU across all nodes in gpupool (`ip link` + `vxlan` MTU)
2) If mixed MTU, schedule controlled MTU normalization or fallback (drain, set vxlan MTU)
3) For RDMA/NIC offload hosts, temporarily disable GRO/GSO on VF if you see ipvs skew
4) If kube-proxy restarts, capture `dmesg` and `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` and open INC
5) Plan kernel update or kube-proxy version that includes ipvs hash fix

jordan: I'll run a rolling change to match MTU on remaining nodes and add an automation check in node-provisioner to fail if MTU mismatch detected.

alex: Please add a note to the infra maintenance calendar — aiming for a low-risk rollout at 02:00 UTC. Also open an incident for tracking.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0452 — preliminary mitigation applied (GSO/GRO disabled on gpu-03, MTU adjusted). Assigned: @maria, @jordan, @vikram.

vikram: I'll write a short postmortem and include kernel workaround + verification steps for RDMA hosts.

maria: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with a PR to node-provisioner to assert MTU consistency and a playbook entry. :thumbsup:

alex: Great. Closing thread for now, will reopen if any regressions.
